claims.event: Native of Wukang in Hu Prefecture. As investigating censor he handled the Wang Tongjiao case and, after pressure from Li Jiao and Li Chengjia, tortured Zhang Zhongzhi into a false confession.

label.en: Attendant Censor of the Left Censorate

claims.event: Implicated for bribery; spared death by Empress Wei's younger sister and exiled as assistant magistrate of Qiongshan.
Transferred to administrator of Kuozhou with regular rank, barred from governing the prefecture, and died.
Reigning emperor. In Shenlong 1, month 1, he was installed; the annal here calls him by the posthumous title Xiaohe.
Relied on the deposed empress's power. The chief ministers feared him. He had the Five Princes exiled and sent Zhou Lizhen to kill them.
The deposed empress whose power Wu Sansi relied on. Her younger sister interceded for Yao Shaozhi.
Killed, with her faction, by Xuanzong in Tanglong 1.
Interceded for Yao Shaozhi after he was sentenced to death for bribery.
Commandant-escort. Plotted to kill Wu Sansi; the plot leaked and he was executed.
With Zu Yanqing, plotted to shoot Wu Sansi. Tortured by Yao Shaozhi, he falsely confessed to rebellion and was executed.

claims.statement: Among the chancellors are those who attach themselves to Sansi.
I will accuse you before the Lord of Heaven.

claims.event: Plotted with Zhang Zhongzhi to shoot Wu Sansi, and married Song Zhisun's wife's younger sister.
Gave his wife's younger sister to Zu Yanqing and thereby learned the plot. His son Tan reported it.

claims.statement: What important business are we undertaking today, that you would take a wife?

claims.event: Her younger sister was given in marriage to Zu Yanqing.
Given in marriage to Zu Yanqing.
Secretly reported his father's knowledge of the plot.
Right censor-in-chief. With Li Jiao he coaxed Yao Shaozhi into changing the case.
Chancellor ordered to join the interrogation. He feared Wu Sansi and helped turn the case.

claims.qualitative: deity invoked in Zhang Zhongzhi's accusation
claims.event: Deity named in Zhang Zhongzhi's speech.
Administrative supervisor of Bianzhou, humiliated by Yao Shaozhi, then appointed investigating censor and ordered to investigate him.
Chief administrator in Yangzhou. Yao Shaozhi told him that Wei Chuanggong's investigation meant death.
Attendant censor at the start of Shenlong. Maternal elder cousin of Cui Shi. Sent by Wu Sansi, he poisoned the exiled princes and was promoted.

label.en: Vice Censor-in-chief of the Left Censorate

claims.event: In Xiantian 1, area commander of Guangzhou. Cui Shi hinted that he kill the exiled Liu Youqiu.

sourceDate.text: 玄宗正位，賜死於桂州驛

claims.event: With Zhang Jianzhi and others, killed Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong and installed Zhongzong.
One of the Five Princes. He distrusted Wu Sansi, confided in Cui Shi, was betrayed, exiled to Lingnan, and poisoned by Zhou Lizhen.
One of the Five Princes, with Huan Yanfan. Exiled to Lingnan and poisoned by Zhou Lizhen.
Secretariat drafter, on good terms with Huan Yanfan and Jing Hui, then betrayed their plan to Wu Sansi and urged that they be killed.
As director of the Secretariat he framed Liu Youqiu and hinted that Zhou Lizhen kill him.
In Tanglong 1 he killed the deposed Empress Wei and her faction.
Upon taking the throne he ordered Zhou Lizhen, Xue Jichang, and Song Zhiwen to die at the Guizhou post station.
Ordered to die with Zhou Lizhen and Song Zhiwen at the Guizhou post station.

sourceDate.text: 玄宗正位，賜死於桂州驛

claims.event: Ordered to die with Zhou Lizhen and Xue Jichang at the Guizhou post station.

sourceDate.text: 玄宗正位，賜死於桂州驛

claims.event: Vice director of the Department of State Affairs. Framed by Cui Shi and marked for death; Wang Jun protected him in Guizhou and he escaped.

label.en: Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs

claims.event: Area commander of Guizhou. Protected Liu Youqiu so that he escaped death.
In Shenlong 1, month 1, beheaded the demoted Zhang Changyi and took the head to the Eastern Capital.
In Tanglong 1, beheaded Zhou Rengui of Bingzhou without waiting for confirmation and took the head to the Western Capital.
In Kaiyuan 2, attendant censor of the Left Censorate. He tortured Lu Chongdao's relatives and had Chongdao and his three sons beaten to death.

label.en: Attendant Censor of the Left Censorate

claims.event: Great-grandfather of Wang Xu. In early Zhenguan, chief minister, and married Princess Yongning.
Wang Gui, great-grandfather of Wang Xu.
Married to Wang Gui in early Zhenguan.
With Huan Yanfan and others, executed Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong and installed Emperor Zhongzong (here called Xiaohe).
Executed by Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan, and others in Shenlong 1, month 1.
Zhang Changzong, executed with Zhang Yizhi. His elder brother was Zhang Changyi.
Elder brother of Zhang Changzong. Already demoted to assistant magistrate of Qianfeng, he was beheaded by Wang Xu.
Chief administrator of Bingzhou and a partisan of the Wei clan. An edict ordered his death; Wang Xu beheaded him at once.
Vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Cui Shi's father-in-law. Demoted, he fled, was caught, and was beaten to death with his three sons.

label.en: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices

claims.event: Wife of Cui Shi and daughter of Lu Chongdao. Named only through that relationship.
Censor-in-chief. After mutual impeachments with Wang Xu he was demoted to prefect of Quzhou.
In Kaiyuan 5 he became director of the Left Office, usually also attendant censor. Sent to Shu, he coerced a magistrate's wife, had the magistrate killed, and took huge bribes.
A slave recorded his bribes. Prince Xian of Song memorialized, and Xu was investigated.
Demoted to assistant magistrate of Longping and died of rage. Contemporaries rejoiced.
In Kaiyuan 6 he sent a slave to expose Wang Xu, then wept before Prince Xian of Song.
Took pity on Ji Xiqiao and memorialized the record. An edict sent the case to the censorate.
Staff officer of the Prince of Song and magistrate of Jiannan County. Reported for bribery, interrogated by Wang Xu, and executed on Xu's memorial.
Wang Xu coerced her because she was beautiful.
Disguised as an imperial messenger, served Wang Xu for months, recorded bribes of several thousand strings, and reported them to Ji Xiqiao.
At the start of Tianbao, assistant magistrate of Xinfeng. Xue Yi introduced him; Xuanzong refused him as a bad character.
In Tianbao 5, through a eunuch, the daughter of his nephew Wu Jingyi became consort of Qi, Prince of Sheng, and Wen was promoted.
In Tianbao 6 he interrogated Yang Shenjin. Li Linfu then promoted him to director in the Ministry of Revenue, with concurrent censor duty.

label.en: Director (langzhong) of the Ministry of Revenue

claims.statement: If you, Third Brother, recommend me as chancellor, I will recommend you and squeeze out Linfu.

claims.unresolvedReason: Ji Jun is named only as Ji Xu's younger brother and Ji Wen's father; this passage gives him no office and no date.
claims.event: Father of Ji Wen and old friend of Shi Jingzhong.

sourceDate.text: 天官侍郎 (the Wu-Zhou title of the vice minister of personnel)

claims.event: Vice minister of personnel. His younger brother Ji Jun was Ji Wen's father.
Literary scholar of the crown prince. He introduced Ji Wen, whom Xuanzong rejected.

label.en: Literary Scholar of the Crown Prince

claims.event: Refused Ji Wen, calling him a bad character.

claims.statement: This is a bad character — I do not want him.

claims.event: Henan intendant. Ji Wen pressed a case that implicated him; Li Linfu suppressed it and Jiong was spared.
As Jingzhao intendant he made Ji Wen assistant magistrate of Wannian. Wen then attached himself to him.
General of the Flying Cavalry. Xiao Jiong waited on him; Ji Wen addressed him familiarly.
Right chancellor. He protected Xiao Jiong, then took Ji Wen into his service to forge cases.
Plotted against the crown prince and had Ji Wen investigate Liu Shi.
Had Yang Shenjin imprisoned and, fearing the case would fail, sent Lu Xuan to plant a prophetic book.
Left chancellor and minister of war. Li Linfu was at odds with him and tried to bring him down through the Ministry of War clerks.
Commandant-escort. Li Linfu was at odds with him. His elder brother Zhang Jun was vice minister of war.
Elder brother of Zhang Ji and vice minister of war.
With Ji Wen, forged cases in the edict-designated prisons for Li Linfu.
Nephew of Ji Wen. His daughter was presented, through a eunuch, as consort of Qi, Prince of Sheng.
Daughter of Wu Jingyi. Made consort of Qi, Prince of Sheng.
Prince of Sheng. Received Wu Jingyi's daughter as consort.
Military-section officer of the Left Militant Guard, husband of Consort Du's younger sister. Li Linfu had Ji Wen investigate him. This unit writes 柳湜; the death notice writes 勣.

label.en: Military-section officer of the Left Militant Guard

claims.event: Liangdi-rank consort. Liu Shi was the husband of her younger sister.
Younger sister of Consort Du; her husband was Liu Shi.
Editorial director. Brought with Wang Xiuji, Lu Ning, and Xu Zheng to the censorate in the Liu Shi case.
Former granary officer of the Right Siyu Guard. Interrogated with Wang Zeng.
Company commander of the Left Militant Guard. Interrogated in the same case.
Cavalry officer of the Left Awesome Guard. Interrogated in the same case.

Vice minister of revenue and concurrent vice censor-in-chief. Wang Hong and Li Linfu accused him of hoarding prophetic texts and of claiming descent from Emperor Yang of Sui. He was imprisoned and then ordered to die with his brothers.
Vice censor-in-chief. Related to Yang Shenjin, but jealous, and he joined in fabricating the case.
Sui emperor. The accusation against Yang Shenjin said Shenjin claimed to be his descendant.

claims.action: named in the charge that Yang Shenjin claimed descent from him

claims.event: Elder brother of Yang Shenjin. Vice director of the Palace Directorate. Captured at the Eastern Capital and later ordered to die with his brothers.

label.en: Vice Director of the Palace Directorate

claims.event: Younger brother of Yang Shenjin and magistrate of Luoyang. Captured at the Eastern Capital and later ordered to die with his brothers.
Learned retainer of Yang Shenjin and old friend of Ji Wen's father. He had held Wen as a child. Forced into a statement that matched Wen's aim, which was then used against Shenjin.

claims.statement: Seventh Brother, give me one sheet of paper.

claims.event: Assistant of Henan. On Ji Wen's order he seized Shi Jingzhong.
Censor. He carried a prophetic book in his sleeve into Yang Shenjin's house and produced it as if found there.

claims.statement: The rebel traitor firmly hid this secret record — now it is obtained!

claims.event: Lesser wife of Yang Shenjin. Lu Xuan pointed her out and beat the terrified household. The text calls her 婢 as well as 小妻.
Enjoyed the emperor's favor. Ji Wen attached himself to him and to Gao Lishi and formed sworn brotherhood with them. Wen addressed him as Third Brother and proposed they push Li Linfu out.
Still powerful at court. Ji Wen formed sworn brotherhood with him and with An Lushan.
In Tianbao 10, deputy military commissioner of Hedong under An Lushan, then prefect of Yanmen, in charge of Anbian coinage, and granted the purple and gold-fish bag.
He went into mourning for his birth mother, and Lushan had him recalled from mourning to his post.
In Tianbao 13, month 1, additionally vice minister of war and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and deputy of the stud, parks, farms, and five pens. He drew closer to Lushan.
Demoted to chief administrator of Liyang, then the next year to assistant magistrate of Gaoyao. He delayed at Shian with Zhang Boji.
The text both says he died in prison and, in the ninth month, that he died at Shixing. Recorded as written.

sourceDate.text: 天寶十四載八月獄中；九月死始興

claims.event: Additionally military commissioner of Hedong. He recommended Ji Wen and later had him recalled from mourning.
In Tianbao 13, month 1, came to court, was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and commissioner of the imperial stud.

label.en: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs

claims.event: In the eleventh month he rebelled. People said it was to avenge Ji Wen. On entering Luoyang he took a usurped throne.
After Xuanzong went to Shu, he found Ji Wen's young son and gave him an office and goods.
Escorted Ji Wen beyond the Fanyang border on his father's order.
Forgot his earlier rejection of Ji Wen after An Lushan praised him.
At Huaqing Palace, on Ji Wen's demotion, he told the court he had been deceived into using Wen.

claims.statement: Ji Wen is the younger kinsman of a harsh official. I was deceived into using him. Now he is gone; you may sleep at ease.

claims.event: Went to Shu after Lushan's rebellion.
Became chancellor. He had long dealt with Ji Wen and recalled him as vice censor-in-chief and investigation commissioner for the capital and Guannei.
Already at odds with Lushan, he resented Ji Wen and had Wei Zhi and Wen impeached. He later sent Jiang Yan to investigate Luo Xishi.
That winter, prefect of Hedong. He used Ji Wen to seek An Lushan's favor and sent local goods as gifts. He confessed and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Guiling.
Assessor. At Yang Guozhong's hint he had a fellow townsman report Wei Zhi.
Judicial officer under Ji Wen. Demoted to assistant magistrate of Xinxing, and in Tianbao 14 was among those at Shian.
Ji Wen relied on him and stopped in Shian. He died at the prefectural gate with Luo Xishi.
Vice director of the Court of State Ceremonial. Luo Xishi was his tang-waisheng.

label.en: Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial

claims.event: In the eighth month, sent to interrogate Ji Wen. Yang Guozhong sent him again to investigate Luo Xishi.

label.en: Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review

claims.event: From Hangzhou, family lately at Luoyang. Tang-waisheng of Zhang Boji. At the start of Tianbao Li Linfu, his marriage relative, set him with Ji Wen to handle prisons. Promoted from censorate chief clerk to palace censor.
In Tianbao 8, vice director then director in the Ministry of Justice.

label.en: Director (langzhong) of the Ministry of Justice

claims.event: In Tianbao 11, after Li Linfu died, sent out as prefect of Zhongbu and Shian and military commissioner of the circuit.
In Tianbao 14 he let exiles at Shian hold temporary posts. He died at the prefectural gate.
Shared Ji Wen's investigation of Yang Shenjin. He had been Wei Jian's judicial officer and betrayed him to Li Linfu, then falsely charged Zhang Xuan.
Testified falsely against Wang Hong in the Xing Zai case. Demoted to chief administrator of Lujiang, he saw Zhang Xuan's ghost and died at once.

claims.statement: The censor-in-chief was about to request five hundred stud horses to aid rebellion, and I did not give them.

claims.event: In Kaiyuan 9, assistant magistrate of Luoyang. With Yan Anzhi he beat prisoners until they seemed ready to die, and only then looked pleased.
In Kaiyuan 18, assistant of Henan. He and Wang Jun were cruel beaters.
Ji Wen went into mourning for her. She is distinguished as the birth mother.
Six or seven years old. After Xuanzong went to Shu, An Lushan appointed him administrator of Henan Prefecture and gave him goods.
Investigated by Ji Wen, with Lu Xuan taking part. Later named among those imprisoned in the cases forged by Luo Xishi and Ji Wen.
Lu Xuan was his judicial officer, then exposed his confession to Li Linfu. Named first among those later imprisoned.
Fellow censor of Lu Xuan. Lu falsely charged him with interpreting prophetic texts together with Yang Shenjin. After Lu's demotion, Lu saw him as a haunting.
Right chancellor. He brought Luo Xishi together with Ji Wen and was related to Luo by marriage.
Lu Xuan was his stud judicial officer. Tried at court over the Xing Zai affair, he died within moments while Lu testified against him.
Named only as the affair (邢縡事) over which Wang Hong was tried.
Imprisoned in a case forged by Luo Xishi and Ji Wen.
Imprisoned in a case forged by Luo Xishi and Ji Wen.
Imprisoned in a case forged by Luo Xishi and Ji Wen. This passage writes 柳勣.
Imprisoned in a case forged by Luo Xishi and Ji Wen.
Imprisoned in a case forged by Luo Xishi and Ji Wen.
Imprisoned in a case forged by Luo Xishi and Ji Wen.
Imprisoned in a case forged by Luo Xishi and Ji Wen.
Exiled to Shian in Tianbao 14. Luo Xishi sometimes gave such exiles temporary posts.
Exiled to Shian in Tianbao 14.
Ordered to replace Luo Xishi as prefect of Shian.

The edict calls him former prefect of Shian and military commissioner, accuses him of installing exiles, demotes him to assistant magistrate of Haikang, and sentences him, with Zhang Boji, to sixty heavy blows.
The same edict condemns him for delay and hiding, and orders sixty heavy blows.
Sentenced to beating. Yuwen Shen was sent to supervise.
Sentenced to beating with Yuan Xi, Wei Jieshe, and Ji Chengen.
Sentenced to beating.
Sentenced to beating.
Rectifier sent to supervise the beatings.

Native of Taiping in Jiangzhou. At the end of Tianbao he was assistant magistrate of Wugong and already more than sixty. With Jing Yu he is later said to have filled the censorate prisons for five or six years, a span longer than the dated career from the recovery of the capitals to his death in Shangyuan 1.
When Suzong recovered the two capitals he was made investigating censor and raised revenue by seizures.
In Qianyuan 2 he fixed the guilt on Xie Yifu. Suzong hid him behind a curtain, and Cui Boyang was exiled.
Assumed the throne at Lingwu.
In the Xie Yifu case he kept Mao Ruoxu behind the curtain, grew angry at Cui Boyang, and had him exiled.

claims.statement: You may go out for now.
If I go out, I will die at once.

claims.event: Pardoned Li Zun because of old merit and only removed him from the Imperial Clan post. Ordered Jing Yu to try Zhen.
Assistant magistrate. Because the crowd was enraged he beat the ward officer to death, and Mao Ruoxu then placed the guilt on him.
Supervisory officer of the seven wards of Fengxiang. He led plundering and was beaten to death by Xie Yifu.
Appealed her husband's death to Li Fuguo.
Received the appeal and had Sun Ying, then Cui Boyang, and then Mao Ruoxu investigate.
Censor. He could not set the case right. Li Xian later sided with him and was demoted.
Vice censor-in-chief and commissioner of the Three Offices. He reproved Mao Ruoxu and was exiled beyond the mountains with more than ten co-investigators.
Chancellor. Demoted because he sided with Sun Ying and the others.
In Tianbao 9, assistant magistrate of Kangcheng. An Sishun brought him onto the Shuofang staff.
Soon after Suzong took the throne at Lingwu he was made investigating censor.
Investigated Li Zun and Zhen, successor Prince of Xue. Zhen was sentenced to death and many associates were executed.
In Baoying 1 he was demoted to prefect of Daozhou. An edict then ordered his execution. He fled and was captured.

claims.statement: When a chief minister enters prison he is a prisoner. Yu, observing ritual, extended a seat — how dare you be disrespectful!
If anyone passes on this record, I regret that I could not investigate the affair. Those who hold prefectural government should not suppress it.

claims.event: Father of Jing Yu. Investigating censor in early Kaiyuan.
Military commissioner of Shuofang. He brought Jing Yu onto his staff.
Heir's junior tutor, director of the Imperial Clan, and Duke of Zheng. Reported by Li Ruobing. Jing Yu forced a confession of bribes. Suzong pardoned him and only removed the Imperial Clan post.
Communications officer of the heir apparent. He reported Li Zun for bribery.
Successor Prince of Xue. He secretly plotted. Jing Yu tried him and he was sentenced to death.
Right Guard general. Beheaded with Cui Chang and others, nine in all.
Acting director of waterways. Beheaded with Dou Rubin and others, nine in all.
Reader of the heir apparent. One of six men beaten to death.
Chief administrator of the Prince of Chen's household. Beaten to death.
Adjutant (sima) of Chuzhou. Beaten to death.
Military-section administrator of the Left Militant Guard. Beaten to death.
Former chief clerk of Mei County. The text gives only the surname Li. Beaten to death.
Presented scholar of the Broad Learning Hall. Beaten to death.
Commandant-escort. Ordered to take his own life.

claims.manner: ordered to take his own life

claims.event: Left regular attendant. Demoted to registrar of Chenzhou.
A foreign merchant with vast assets. Yang Guozhong, as chancellor, appointed him protector-general of Annan. The sentence gives no year; the post is stated before his Zhide office.
In the Zhide era, acting chief minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, managing the eastern route south of the mountains.

label.en: Acting Chief Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial

claims.event: Accused of secretly communicating with Shi Chaoyi. Tortured until he looked inhuman, then executed and his assets confiscated.
Right chancellor in the year-14 case that this edict continues. Kang Qian's biography says that, as chancellor, he appointed Kang protector-general of Annan; that appointment is not itself dated.
Kang Qian was accused of secretly communicating with him.
Served with Bi Yao as a cruel censor. The age named Mao, Jing, Pei, and Bi together. Pei and Bi were exiled to central Qian.
Served with Pei Sheng as a cruel censor and was exiled to central Qian.

translationRepairs: Upon leaving the purple he served as ceremonial officer, and through repeated promotions was appointed Investigating Censor.
Upon entering service he served as ceremonial officer, and through repeated promotions was appointed Investigating Censor.
解褐 means doffing a commoner's hemp robe to enter office, not leaving the purple.
Under Emperor Zhongzong, Wu Sansi relied on the deposed empress's power, and Chief Commandant of Horse Wang Tongjiao plotted to kill him.
Under Emperor Zhongzong, Wu Sansi relied on the deposed empress's power, and Wang Tongjiao, the commandant-escort plotted to kill him.
駙馬都尉 is the commandant-escort (an imperial son-in-law), not a commandant of horse.
In the reign of Emperor Zhongzong, Wu Sansi relied on the deposed empress's power; Chief Commandant of Horse Wang Tongjiao plotted to execute him.
In the reign of Emperor Zhongzong, Wu Sansi relied on the deposed empress's power; Wang Tongjiao, the commandant-escort plotted to execute him.
駙馬都尉 is the commandant-escort (an imperial son-in-law), not a commandant of horse.
He was repeatedly promoted to Left Censor.
He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Censor of the Left Censorate.
左臺侍御史 is an attendant censor (侍御史) of the Left Censorate, not a generic left censor.
Through repeated promotions he was made Left Censor.
Through repeated promotions he was made Attendant Censor of the Left Censorate.
左臺侍御史 is an attendant censor (侍御史) of the Left Censorate, not a generic left censor.
On a mission to the lower Yangtze he passed through Bian Prefecture and publicly humiliated Army Records Officer Wei Chuanggong.
